[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Chuck Robb]] ran for re-election to a third term but was defeated by former [[Governor of Virginia|Virginia governor]] [[George Allen (American politician)|George Allen]].{{cite web | url=http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=51&year=2000&f=0&elect=0&off=3&class=1 | title= 2000 Senatorial General Election Results - Virginia | publisher= uselectionatlas.org | author= David Leip | date= January 1, 2012 | access-date=March 4, 2013}}{{cite web | url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=118 | title= Our Campaigns - VA US Senate Race - Nov 07, 2000 | publisher= ourcampaigns.com | author= Our Campaigns | date= April 23, 2004 | access-date=March 4, 2013}} {{As of|2026}}, this is the last time that Republicans won the Class 1 Senate seat in Virginia. == General election == === Candidates === * [[George Allen (American politician)|George Allen]], former [[governor of Virginia]] and former U.S. representative from [[Chesterfield County, Virginia|Chesterfield County]] (Republican) * [[Chuck Robb]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1989 and former [[governor of Virginia]] (Democratic) ===Debates=== *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159395-1/virginia-senatorial-debate Complete video of debate], September 24, 2000 *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159404-1/virginia-senatorial-debate Complete video of debate], September 25, 2000 *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159948-1/virginia-senate-debate Complete video of debate], October 22, 2000 === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" ! scope="col" |Poll source ! scope="col" |Date(s) ! scope="col" style="width:75px;" |Sample
